evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, DateTime.DaysInMonth(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month)).AddDays days
| true, days when days >= 1 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule is in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The terms wording is in Summa.Ledger. The record codec is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). The form parsing and its validation are in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). The diff touches no Tier 3 or Tier 4 code, so nothing is decided above Tier 2.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no clock, randomness, I/O or persistence call. The new code is pure: DateOnly arithmetic, Int32.TryParse with the invariant culture, and JSON encode and decode. Tier 1/2 gains no effect.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The words "Net {days} EOM" are written out in two places, Documents.termsText and Invoicing.termsWords. The existing Net wording was already duplicated the same way. The 1 to 365 limit is restated in the new EOM branch, next to the existing Net branch. The copies agree, so this is restatement and not drift. The error text is now a single local `termsError` shared by both branches.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule and the ordinal wording are in Summa.Ledger. The range check and the codec are in Summa.Storage and Summa.Web.Engine, which are both Tier 2. Tier 3 and Tier 4 are not touched.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds only pure code: date arithmetic, string formatting, parsing and JSON decoding. It adds no effect anywhere, and none below Tier 4.

evidence.quote: if day >= 1 && day <= 28 then Ok(DayOfNextMonth day)
| true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The ordinal wording "Due the Nth of next month" has one definition, `dayOfNextMonthText`, and both Documents.termsText and Invoicing.termsWords call it. That is better than the EOM wording. The 1 to 28 limit, however, is hard-coded in two places, the storage decoder and the form parser, with no shared constant, so the two could drift. The "Net {days} EOM" wording is still duplicated, as it was before this change. The copies currently agree.
